title: Service error surge mitigation: triage, graded fallbacks, and rollback runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During a recent customer escalation we observed a multi-tenant surge that produced a cascade of server-side errors and long tail request timeouts across our public inference endpoints. This ticket captures the investigation notes, immediate mitigations applied, the short-term rollback and canary strategy, and a proposed medium-term fix to prevent recurrence. The goal is to restore steady-state customer traffic with minimal invalid responses and to provide a reproducible playbook for future surges.
acceptance_criteria: Customer-visible error rate reduced to pre-incident baseline (<0.2% 5xx across active tenants)
No more than 2 customers with degraded latency beyond SLO without targeted communication
Automated slow-start routing and per-tenant cooling policy validated in canary and rolled to prod
Postmortem with RCA and 3 concrete engineering actions landed within 7 days
steps_taken: Scoped the blast radius using request-id traces and tenant tags — identified ~12 heavy tenants contributing 78% of error tail
Temporarily increased API-level circuit breaker thresholds for low-priority routes to avoid mass-fast-fail churn
Enabled per-tenant request shaping in the edge proxy for the top 5 noisy tenants and applied 30s soft-queueing
Pushed a hotfix to reduce connection pool max-lifetime from 10m to 2m to avoid socket exhaustion during surges (rolled to 10% then 100%)
Applied KV-cache compaction on a subset of serving nodes to reduce memory amplification from long-lived prefixes
Deployed a rapid rollback for the recently deployed kernel selector change that correlated with higher tail latencies (rolled back in <20 minutes)
analysis_and_findings: Root cause appears to be a confluence: (1) spike in concurrent long-sequence requests from a few tenants, (2) a recent kernel selector optimization that increased single-request CPU jitter under certain sequence distributions, (3) proxy connection reuse bug causing head-of-line stalls
Amplification vector: client SDK retry semantics caused parallel retries of inflight requests when responses exceeded 10s, creating retry storms—our circuit breakers were opening too late
KV cache thrash increased GC pressure on GPUs which in turn lengthened host-side request latencies and pushed more requests into retry windows
proposed_medium_term_fixes: Introduce tenant-priority routing with explicit soft-fallback models for noisy tenants (lower-cost quantized variants) and automated downgrade policies
Tighten back-pressure at the edge: implement token-bucket admission with per-tenant hysteresis and probabilistic early-drop for low priority requests
Harmonize SDK retry semantics with server-side idempotency tokens and recommended client-side backoff windows in the developer portal
Add a kernel-selection regression test in the CI harness that simulates heavy long-sequence distributions and measures tail CPU jitter
Fix proxy connection reuse bug and add connection lifecycle telemetry (open/close/idle time distribution) to the Console dashboard
next_steps: Complete PR to add per-tenant downgrade policy engine (ENG-48292 will track the implementation)
Run a controlled canary of the admission token-bucket on a non-production region for 48h
Coordinate communications with account success for the top affected customers; share mitigation steps and ETA for permanent fixes
Draft postmortem (owner: Aisha). Include timelines, customer impact table, and follow-up owners
blockers: Need sandbox infra with representative long-sequence workload for reliable canary testing
Dependency on networking team to push proxy connection lifecycle patch (PR# 6124) through security review
